intended_object: For a multispan diagram I (objects L_a, R_b and maps snd_a : L_a → R_{snd a}), this is the canonical morphism ∐_a L_a → ∐_b R_b whose restriction to the a-th summand is snd_a followed by the coproduct inclusion. It is stated for any chosen colimit cofan of the left objects and any cofan of the right objects. The intended object comes from the docstring and from how the map is used for the multicoequalizer-as-coequalizer construction.
explanation: The body uses the universal property of the colimit cofan c (`Cofan.IsColimit.desc hc`) to build the map from the family `I.snd i ≫ d.inj _`. This is the standard map induced on coproducts. The lemma `inj_sndSigmaMapOfIsColimit` confirms that it agrees with `I.snd i ≫ d.inj _` on each summand. It is the dual of the existing `fstSigmaMapOfIsColimit`, and `sndSigmaMap` specializes it to the chosen coproducts `∐`. Only c needs to be a colimit; d can be any cofan. That is the most general sensible hypothesis, since the target of the map does not need a universal property. The generality is right: an arbitrary category, an arbitrary multispan shape, and no existence assumption on coproducts.
